name: Cleveland Cavaliers
notes: The Cleveland Cavaliers compete in the NBA's Eastern Conference, Central Division, and play home games at Rocket Arena in downtown Cleveland. Core colors are wine, gold, navy, and black. The team is built around a young frontcourt duo (Evan Mobley, Jarrett Allen) and All-Star guard Donovan Mitchell, coming off a franchise-record 64-win season in 2024-25 and a Central Division title, with James Harden re-signing in 2026 free agency to bolster the backcourt.

roster.facts: Seven-time All-Star and franchise cornerstone who signed a four-year, $273 million extension in July 2026 to remain Cleveland's leading man.
roster.name: Donovan Mitchell

roster.facts: Reigning 2025 NBA Defensive Player of the Year and first-time All-Star, anchoring Cleveland's frontcourt on a max rookie extension worth up to $269 million.
roster.name: Evan Mobley

roster.facts: Future Hall of Famer who re-signed with Cleveland on a three-year, $97 million deal in 2026 free agency after averaging 8.0 assists last season.
roster.name: James Harden

roster.facts: Starting center and 2022 All-Star who battled a broken finger and knee tendinitis in 2025-26 while averaging 15.4 points and 8.5 rebounds.
roster.name: Jarrett Allen

roster.facts: Acquired via a five-team sign-and-trade in August 2026 on a four-year, $88 million deal, immediately slotting in as Cleveland's starting small forward.
roster.name: Peyton Watson

roster.facts: Breakout second-year forward who earned 35 starts, a Rising Stars nod, and averaged 13.2 points on 44.6% three-point shooting in 2025-26.
roster.name: Jaylon Tyson

roster.facts: Cleveland's top marksman signed a four-year, $38 million deal in 2025 and rewarded it by shooting 42.1% from three in 2025-26.
roster.name: Sam Merrill

roster.facts: Cleveland's top backup point guard behind Harden, with the Cavs exercising his fourth-year team option in June 2026 to keep him through 2026-27.
roster.name: Craig Porter Jr.

roster.facts: Veteran backup center brought back on a one-year deal to bolster frontcourt depth after averaging 6.2 points on 50.6% shooting in limited minutes.
roster.name: Thomas Bryant

roster.facts: Former No. 5 overall pick making an NBA comeback after six years starring in EuroLeague, signing a one-year, $2.8 million deal in July 2026.
roster.name: Mario Hezonja

roster.facts: Duke product taken 49th overall in the 2025 draft, developing as a depth guard on a four-year deal with two seasons fully guaranteed.
roster.name: Tyrese Proctor

roster.facts: Arkansas freshman and McDonald's All-American drafted 34th overall in 2026, signing a four-year, $9.3 million rookie contract.
roster.name: Meleek Thomas

roster.facts: Athletic forward whose two-way deal was converted to a standard NBA contract in February 2026 after strong G League production.
roster.name: Nae'Qwan Tomlin

roster.facts: Senegalese center and 2022 second-round pick just signed September 2, 2026 after three seasons starring for Baskonia in Spain's ACB/EuroLeague.
roster.name: Khalifa Diop

roster.facts: Two-way forward who earned his roster spot in January 2026 after averaging 19.4 points for the G League's Cleveland Charge.
roster.name: Tristan Enaruna

roster.facts: Undrafted Miami center signed to a two-way contract in July 2026, splitting time between Cleveland and the G League Charge.
roster.name: Ernest Udeh Jr.

roster.facts: Two-way forward and deepest bench piece, having starred for the Cleveland Charge with 19.3 points a game before signing in February 2026.
roster.name: Riley Minix
